faqs.q: Do your instructors speak Urdu or Punjabi?
faqs.a: Yes. All our instructors speak English, Urdu and Punjabi, so you can learn in the language you are most comfortable with.

faqs.q: Do you teach on evenings and weekends?
faqs.a: Yes. Lessons run 7 days a week, from 9am to 9pm.

faqs.q: Can I use your car for my test?
faqs.a: Ask us before you book. We need to check the instructor and car are free on your date, and we will tell you about any test day charge.

faqs.q: Can you book my driving test for me?
faqs.a: No. Since 12 May 2026 only the learner can book, change or cancel a car test on GOV.UK. We help you decide when you are ready and plan your lessons around the date.

faqs.q: Will I fail if I take a wrong turn on the test?
faqs.a: No. A wrong turn is not marked as a fault. The examiner will help you get back on the route.

faqs.q: What should I bring to my first lesson?
faqs.a: Bring your provisional licence and any glasses or contact lenses you need for driving. You must be able to read a number plate from 20 metres.

faqs.q: How old do I need to be to start?
faqs.a: You can apply for a provisional licence at 15 years and 9 months and usually start driving a car at 17.

faqs.q: Why choose Manchester One as your driving school in Manchester?
faqs.a: As a driving school in Manchester built around patient, DVSA approved teaching, we focus on real driving confidence rather than just passing a test. With a 5.0 Google rating and lessons available across Manchester, Bolton, Salford, Trafford, Oldham and Rochdale, your lessons follow your own progress rather than a fixed script.

faqs.q: Which driving test centre is easiest?
faqs.a: No test centre guarantees an easier test. Traffic, routes and conditions vary. Preparing for different situations matters more than relying on one supposedly easy route.

faqs.q: I already drive overseas. Do I need beginner lessons?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. An assessment identifies which UK road habits or practical test requirements need work.

faqs.q: Can I change from manual to automatic?
faqs.a: Yes. If clutch and gear control are taking too much attention, an automatic lesson lets you compare the two before deciding.

faqs.q: Can I switch driving instructor?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us what training you have already completed and what you still find difficult. An assessment can establish your current level without automatically starting you from scratch.

faqs.q: Can I start before passing my theory test?
faqs.a: Yes. You can start practical lessons with a valid provisional licence. You need to pass your theory test before taking your practical test.

faqs.q: Do you cover my area?
faqs.a: Yes, if you live in Manchester, Bolton, Salford, Trafford, Oldham, Rochdale or Stockport. Send us your postcode to confirm instructor availability and your hourly rate.

faqs.q: How much are driving lessons in Manchester?
faqs.a: Lessons cost £37 or £39 per hour depending on your postcode. Manual and automatic cost the same, and the shortest session is 90 minutes.

faqs.q: How many driving lessons will I need?
faqs.a: There's no fixed number that applies to everyone. Previous experience, lesson frequency, private practice and how consistently you can drive without help all affect how much tuition you may need.

faqs.q: What Brings You Here?
faqs.a: You do not need to fit into a standard beginner lesson plan. Start with the situation that sounds most like yours.

faqs.q: Not sure which area applies to you?
faqs.a: Click the button to enter your postcode and check local lesson availability and pricing options. Check My Area We'll use your postcode to show the most relevant lesson prices and availability.

faqs.q: Manual or Automatic?
faqs.a: You do not need a long technical explanation before choosing. Understand the difference and pick the option that suits your goals. MANUAL

faqs.q: Not Sure Which To Choose?
faqs.a: Try an assessment rather than guessing. YOUR LEARNING JOURNEY

Ready to start your driving journey? Contact Manchester One Driving School today to ask about lesson prices, check instructor availability, or book your first session. Our team is here to help you every day of the week, from early morning right through to the evening. All our instructors speak English, Urdu and Punjabi.

Whether you’re a complete beginner or looking to switch instructors, getting in touch is the first step. We’ll listen to what you need, match you with a DVSA-approved instructor in your area, and get you booked in quickly. You can reach us by phone, email, WhatsApp, or the contact form below, whichever works best for you.
We follow official DVSA learning standards across every lesson, so when you contact Manchester One Driving School, you’re speaking to a team that genuinely understands what it takes to help you pass.
Searching for a driving school in Manchester you can trust? We offer patient manual and automatic lessons across Greater Manchester.
Whether you are a beginner, nervous learner, changing instructors or preparing for your test, we help you understand the right next step.
You will be driving without an instructor for years afterwards.
That is why your lessons should prepare you for more than one test route.

Whether you’re learning in busy Manchester traffic, residential streets in Trafford, faster roads around Bolton, or the roundabouts and junctions across Salford, Oldham, Rochdale and Stockport, the goal is the same: learn how to read the road and make safe decisions for yourself.
We do not want you to simply remember what to do when an instructor gives you a prompt.
As a driving school in Manchester serving learners across Greater Manchester, we know the busy roads, roundabouts and junctions around your local test centre.
We want you to understand the situation, respond confidently and develop driving skills you can use long after test day.
Our instructors live and teach across Greater Manchester, from Cheetham Hill to Chadderton to Bolton, with genuine local road knowledge.
Each lesson builds on the last with clear feedback, so you always know what you are working on and how close you are to test-ready.
Book lessons at times that fit around work, college or family commitments, with instructors covering evenings and weekends.

Manual driving can feel like too much at once: clutch, gears and the road together. Keep working on manual control, or try an automatic lesson before deciding.
Stalling, roundabouts, busy roads or a previous bad experience can make driving feel overwhelming. Start at a pace that helps you understand the problem, practise safely and build confidence.
Changing instructor does not mean starting again. Your previous lessons still matter. We assess what you already know, identify what is holding you back and focus on the next steps.
